#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: --job-name=100c100
#flux: -q stampede

# The original Slurm script used a job array.
#flux: --array=0-2

# The original script did not specify nodes, tasks, or CPUs, so it defaults to 1 task with 1 CPU.
# This is preserved in the Flux translation.
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1

# The Slurm output format is translated to Flux equivalents.
# {job.name} corresponds to %x (implied), {job.id} to %A, and {array.task_id} to %a.
#flux: -o /home-mscluster/npather/disentangle/100c100.{job.id}.{array.task_id}.txt

# Each task in the job array will execute this command independently.
# The command appears to be truncated in the original script ('--evaluat').
# This has been preserved as is.
python3 main.py \
--aicrowd_challenge=false \
--name=100c100 \
--alg=BetaVAE \
--traverse_z=true \
--traverse_c=true \
--dset_dir=/home-mscluster/npather/disentanglement-pytorch/data/dsprites \
--dset_name=dsprites_full \
--encoder=PadlessGaussianConv64 \
--decoder=SimpleConv64 \
--discriminator=SimpleDiscriminator \
--z_dim=20 \
--use_wandb=true \
--w_kld=1.0 \
--w_tc=9.0 \
--lr_G=0.001 \
--lr_scheduler=ReduceLROnPlateau \
--lr_scheduler_args mode=min factor=0.95 patience=1 min_lr=0.00005 \
--max_iter=90000 \
--iterations_c=90000 \
--max_c=100 \
--evaluat \
--evaluation_metric mig sap_score irs dci beta_vae_sklearn factor_vae_metric \
--alg=BetaVAE \
--loss_terms \
--use_bandit=false \
--controlled_capacity_increase=true \
--loss_txt=false \
--wandb_project_name=anneal \
--qma_alpha=0.001 \
--boltzmann_lambda=15 \

reasons: Validation failed at directive: --array=0-2. The job array feature is not part of the core Flux scheduler specification and is often implemented as a site-specific extension; this directive is not universally valid.
issues: The python command is syntactically incorrect. It contains a truncated argument (`--evaluat`) which will cause the script to fail. It also specifies the `--alg` argument twice.
The script is non-portable due to multiple hardcoded, user-specific absolute paths for the output file and dataset directory.
The job does not request any specific memory or GPU resources. For a deep learning job, this is highly unusual and will likely lead to failure due to insufficient resources.

#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: --job-name=100c100
#flux: -q stampede

# The original script did not specify nodes, tasks, or CPUs, so it defaults to 1 task with 1 CPU.
# This is preserved for the single job that will run the serial loop.
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1

# This single output file will capture any output from the main script itself.
# Output from each python run is redirected inside the loop.
#flux: -o /home-mscluster/npather/disentangle/100c100.{job.id}.log

# CRITICAL: The original Slurm job array (--array=0-2) has been converted to a serial for-loop.
# This means each task will run one after another, NOT in parallel.
# The total runtime of this job will be the sum of the runtimes of the individual tasks.

for i in $(seq 0 2); do
    echo "--- Starting Serial Task ID: $i ---"
    output_file="/home-mscluster/npather/disentangle/100c100.${FLUX_JOB_ID:-0}.${i}.txt"
    
    # The command appears to be truncated in the original script ('--evaluat').
    # This has been preserved as is.
    python3 main.py \
    --aicrowd_challenge=false \
    --name=100c100 \
    --alg=BetaVAE \
    --traverse_z=true \
    --traverse_c=true \
    --dset_dir=/home-mscluster/npather/disentanglement-pytorch/data/dsprites \
    --dset_name=dsprites_full \
    --encoder=PadlessGaussianConv64 \
    --decoder=SimpleConv64 \
    --discriminator=SimpleDiscriminator \
    --z_dim=20 \
    --use_wandb=true \
    --w_kld=1.0 \
    --w_tc=9.0 \
    --lr_G=0.001 \
    --lr_scheduler=ReduceLROnPlateau \
    --lr_scheduler_args mode=min factor=0.95 patience=1 min_lr=0.00005 \
    --max_iter=90000 \
    --iterations_c=90000 \
    --max_c=100 \
    --evaluat \
    --evaluation_metric mig sap_score irs dci beta_vae_sklearn factor_vae_metric \
    --alg=BetaVAE \
    --loss_terms \
    --use_bandit=false \
    --controlled_capacity_increase=true \
    --loss_txt=false \
    --wandb_project_name=anneal \
    --qma_alpha=0.001 \
    --boltzmann_lambda=15 > "${output_file}" 2>&1

    echo "--- Finished Serial Task ID: $i ---"
done

issues: CRITICAL: The original parallel job array, which would have run three tasks simultaneously, has been converted into a serial for-loop. This is a fundamental change in execution that will dramatically increase the total time to completion, as the tasks will now run one after another instead of concurrently.

The job does not request any specific memory or GPU resources. For a deep learning job involving models like BetaVAE, this is highly unusual and will almost certainly lead to failure due to insufficient memory or the absence of a required GPU.
The python command is syntactically incorrect. It contains a truncated argument (`--evaluat`) which will likely cause the script to fail. It also specifies the `--alg` argument twice.
The script is non-portable due to multiple hardcoded, user-specific absolute paths for the output files and dataset directory.
